title: Nils Stotz (Bocconi lecturer) takes the book's emergent-intelligence idea to AI — 'We are adding intelligence to organizations faster than we are redesigning how that intelligence coordinates'
summary: A product lead and Bocconi lecturer picks up the book's framing of organizations as emergent intelligence — the ant-and-maze experiment where the colony develops a short-term memory no individual ant has — and turns it on enterprise AI. His argument: companies are adding capability at the individual level, in private chats and fragmented workflows, which produces more local intelligence without a more intelligent organization.
blockquote: I recently read Eric Ries's new book, Incorruptible. One idea I found particularly interesting was his description of organizations as a form of “emergent intelligence”: the whole can develop capabilities that do not exist in any individual member.
attribution_title: Head of Product · Lecturer and researcher, Bocconi · Springer author
